fatal_errors: The proposed material is an unspecified compositionally graded Cu-rich HEA rather than the target FeNiCrCoCu HEA coating adhered directly to a Cu matrix.
The hypothesis replaces the target nanoindentation and friction study across 300–1200 K with a deposition and adhesion-engineering proposal.
It omits the critical 900 K transition, including lattice disorder, dislocation-density reduction, hardness and modulus loss, and increased friction.

Neither cited source demonstrates a Cu-rich graded HEA interlayer on Cu or validates the claimed adhesion mechanism; E1 concerns a refractory HEA coating on steel, while E2 provides only general HEA background.
explanation: The response addresses the broad coating-on-Cu theme and offers a testable engineering alternative, but it does not reconstruct the material, simulation, temperature conditions, mechanism, or quantitative outcomes of the target. Its control-based adhesion experiment could test its own proposition, yet it would not distinguish the target temperature-dependent transition from stacking-fault-mediated deformation to lattice disorder. The cited evidence supports general HEA coating utility and metallurgical bonding in another substrate system, not the specific graded Cu-rich interlayer claim, so the alternative remains scientifically conceivable but inadequately supported.
